before: Fix a starting point $(x_0,y_0)$ and any target first coordinate $u\in[0,1)$. For each $n\in\mathbb Z$, the flow parameter $s=n-x_0+u$ makes the first coordinate equal to $u$ modulo one and the second equal to $y_0+a(n-x_0+u)$ modulo one. The residues $na\bmod1$ are dense: for any integer $N\ge2$, divide $[0,1)$ into $N$ half-open intervals of length $1/N$. Two of the $N+1$ residues $0,a,\ldots,Na\bmod1$ lie in one interval, so for some nonzero integer $k$ and integer $r$ we have $0<\delta:=|ka-r|<1/N$; the strict lower bound follows from irrationality. Replacing $k$ by $-k$ if needed, $\delta$ is an integer multiple of $a$ modulo one. The residues $j\delta$ for $j=0,1,\ldots,\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$ have gaps at most $\delta$ around the unit interval, so they form a $1/N$-net. Since $N$ is arbitrary, the multiples of $a$ are dense modulo one. Therefore the orbit is dense in the second coordinate for the chosen $u$; as $u$ was arbitrary, the flow orbit is dense in $T^2$.

before: Define $I(t):=\int_t^\infty e^{(t-s)/\tau_e}F_{\rm ext}(s)\,ds$, interpreting the integral as a finite Riemann integral after any upper truncation beyond $\max\{t,T\}$; compact support makes the value independent of that truncation. For $t<T$, write $I(t)=e^{t/\tau_e}\int_t^T e^{-s/\tau_e}F_{\rm ext}(s)\,ds$. By [F1] the integrand is integrable on this compact interval, and [F2] together with the fundamental theorem gives $$ I'(t)=-F_{\rm ext}(t)+\frac{1}{\tau_e}I(t)\qquad (t<T). $$ For $a=I/(m\tau_e)$ this identity becomes $\tau_e a'= -F_{\rm ext}/m+a$, which rearranges to the displayed Abraham–Lorentz equation. For $t>T$, both $I$ and $F_{\rm ext}$ vanish, so the same equation holds. At $t=T$, smoothness and support imply $F_{\rm ext}(T)=0$, and the one-sided derivatives agree with the displayed identity.

Along the full solution put $h(\tau)=\eta(U,U)+c^2$; then $$ h'(\tau)=2\eta(U,a_{\rm LL})=\frac{2\tau_e}{c^2}\eta(U,B)h(\tau). $$ The coefficient is continuous. The zero function solves this scalar linear IVP with $h(0)=0$, and the scalar vector field is locally Lipschitz in $h$ because it is linear in that variable, so uniqueness [F5] gives $h=0$ on the full common interval. Thus the proper-time normalization $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ is preserved.
